clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1991–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's death in June 1991, within three years: you left home for the conservatory in September 1991, leaned hard on your friend Rafe, then hurt your wrist in October and couldn't play; you and Rafe clashed in November and he moved out; you were on your own getting high through the winter, then lost and low in January 1992 with your grandfather gone and your mother about to remarry, unable to get going; your grandmother Winifred was treated for a thyroid tumour around the same time; you spent a bleak year at community college through 1992, then found your drive again with an exchange to Portugal in early 1994 and raced through the rest of your degree. Your mother filled in your college forms in March 1991, you underfunctioning; your sister Tara was born in July 1990. Your cousin Bella was treated for melanoma in early 1994. The shifts pile up around your grandfather's stroke and death, your leaving home, the loss of playing, and your own low functioning through those years.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's death, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer found in 2001 or 2002, within three years: you were running out of steam for performing from September 2001, less content by the month; you had a disastrous audition for the national orchestra in early 2002 and were done with performing; you were on poor terms with family and friends from September 2002 onward; you left Thornbury for Gull Harbour in September 2002, met Marisol at a winter party in early 2003, left Gull Harbour to live with her in June 2003, then split up with her in October 2003 and sank into a deep depression; you returned to Thornbury in November 2003, could not face your family, relied on friends instead, and were anxious; you began swimming laps in January 2004, requested help from your parents with therapy costs that month, and returned to your therapist; your grandmother spent her final months in your parents' home in September 2003 and died of bowel cancer in February 2004. You dropped in on her briefly, hung over, in January 2004 on your way to the airport, anxious and distant. The shifts pile up around your loss of performing, your distance from family, your failed relationship, and your grandmother's illness and death across those years.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008–2010
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within two years: your grandfather Clifford died in January 2008, the year uncertain; you took four weeks building with Silas at Alder Creek in July 2008 and were too drained for conversation with your mother; she pressed you to visit in late July and you kept the door shut on her when she came regardless; you left for nursing school in August 2008 and stopped speaking to your mother when you relocated to Marlow Sound in September, a silence that held for roughly a year; your aunt Imogen had a stroke in January 2009 with months of rehabilitation ahead. The shifts pile up around your grandparents' deaths, your move away to nursing school, and your cutoff from your mother across those months.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within two and a half years: you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along; your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in October 2017; your sister Tara was married in summer 2018 and was expecting her first child by October 2019, Russell's first grandchild that you know of; your aunt Imogen's memory slipped and worsened from 2015 onward, and by October 2018 she lashed out when muddled; your mother had a heart check-up after her siblings' illnesses in October 2018, all clear; your job steadied and paid well by June 2019, anxiety down; by October 2019 you felt you ought to be driving your projects forward, constantly anxious; you started a sleeping pill in October 2019, anxiety down though sleep itself no better; you aimed for shorter, more regular calls with your mother to soften the distance; at the same time in late October 2019, Wren was swamped one thing after another with a street party, fundraising dinner, and drive to the lake for her mother's retirement party; you were too strict laying out a plan to settle her, and she settled once the weekend had a plan; the dinner went well; at the lake weekend on October 23rd you awoke from the small hours with no more sleep and could only pull back as the others rose, anxious and distant, feeling you don't belong; Wren was anxious when you'd had no sleep at family occasions, long quiet drives home afterward. The shifts pile up around your marriage, your wife's family occasions, your own anxious state, and distance at family gatherings across those months.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
